fluid.jit.plotter aims for speed with large datasets (– check the last tab).
Using the refer message instead of a dictionary avoids some copying and gives you several times the load speed with large datasets.
Nevertheless, the dictionary input still works, just like with fluid.plotter.
refer without arguments resets all colors to black
refer without arguments erases the plot

The right inlet expects the name of a fluid.labelset~ with the refer message.
Each unique label in the fluid.labelset~ will be randomly assigned to a colour inside the fluid.plotter.
Use the refer message with the name of a fluid.dataset~. The fluid.dataset~ must be only two dimensions.
pointsize to control individual point sizes
pointcolor will set an RGBA color to a point (referenced by dataset ID)
clear and reset are aliases to refer with no args
colorscheme message is redirected to [p labels2colors]
refer (to a dataset) or highlight (list of IDs)
bang when created dict with color palette
only let mousing through if there is a dataset reference

We also store these as the ranges defined before click'n'drag zooming.

Drawing through the "advanced" interface lets you draw at a lower level.

Set the size of each point.
Format is:
<identifer>
<size>

Set the pointcolor of each point. Format is:
<identifier>
<r><g><b><a>
You don't need a fluid.dataset~ necessarily. Using the setpoint message you can create a plot point by point.
generate a random set of points.

Change the shape of the points as they're drawn.

fluid.jit.plotter really shines with very large datasets. Since it is based on a jit.gl.render instead of jsui, it can take datasets with millions of points and highlight thousands without much lag.
alter the amount or direction of the panning (when shift + dragging).
generate a random set of points.
The range of the generated data sits between -2.5 and 2.5 but the view of the data is set to be between -5 and 5 on both axes to have some whitespace around the edges.
fluid.jit.plotter has a zoom feature allowing you to zone in on subsets of the plot
The selected range is output from the right in response to drag + modifier events.

You can interactively control the range of the x and y areas using different keyboard modifiers while clicking and dragging.

If you (hold option / alt / winkey + drag) a box will be drawn over the canvas, showing which area of the plot you will "zoom" in on in.

If you (control + drag) it resets the x and y ranges to the last stored values received from a message (such as range [-5 5]).

If you (shift + drag) you can pan the view around within the current zoom range.

Click these messages to start adjusting the range to the minimum and maximum of the original data. You will see that the data is now visible in the space. Wiggle the number boxes to see how it affects the display of points.
You'll notice that there is nothing in the plotter. By default it is displaying the 0 to 1 range in both dimensions.

By default, the range of the fluid.jit.plotter is between 0 and 1 for both the X and Y axis. You can modify the displayed range of the plotter with two messages, xrange and yrange. Each message accepts two values, the minimum and maximum for each.
Generate random data between a range that is not normal. In this case the horizontal values range between 0 and 10000, and the vertical values range between 40 and 600.
